HOLD: `typeof null === 'object'` is still true in all modern engines, including current Node versions and browsers. ES6 did not change it.

This was explicitly decided NOT to be fixed—changing it would break existing code. It's documented as a known quirk that persists for backward compatibility. You can verify it in any JavaScript environment today:

```javascript
typeof null === 'object'  // true
```

The guard `v !== null && typeof v === 'object'` remains necessary.

What would change my mind: a link to official spec or engine source showing this changed.
